description: ODC: serious block reuse - the SAME authored block instantiated in DIFFERENT screens, each with ITS OWN arguments, and the same block reused INSIDE another block. WfCovPriceTag is the reusable piece: four inputs (Label and Amount mandatory, Currency and Emphasis optional with DefaultValue) and an IPlaceholderWidget Footnote, the extension point that each consumer fills with its own content. WfCovPolicyCard instantiates it TWICE inside itself, with different arguments (premium vs deductible): the first does not write Currency and keeps the block's own default EUR, the second writes USD - reuse inside a BLOCK, with no screen in the path. On top of that, TWO screens instantiate the SAME WfCovPolicyCard: WfCovPolicyDetail passes a screen variable and literals, WfCovPolicySummary passes another policy and an EXPRESSION (RenewalPremium * 1.15); both instances are called WfCovPolicyCard1, which proves that the instance name belongs to the PARENT and not to the block. WfCovPolicySummary also instantiates WfCovPriceTag DIRECTLY through the visual authoring of section 3.5 (`<Block name :Input>` with `<slot name="Footnote">` to fill the placeholder), to show that the same block is reused through both authoring paths and at two levels on the same screen. The proof closes in the `usages`: WfCovPriceTag has 3 instances (two inside IMobileBlock:WfCovPolicyCard, one inside IMobileScreen:WfCovPolicySummary) and WfCovPolicyCard has 2, in different screens. TWO THINGS THAT ONLY SHOW UP WHEN READING BACK. (1) Inheriting the default is NOT having no argument: the platform creates one IArgument per parameter when instantiating, and the one of WfCovPriceTag1 exists with an empty Value - which is why the `usages` of Currency counts the same 3 arguments as that of Amount, and whoever counts arguments to know who passed a value counts wrong; the Value decides. (2) The content of a placeholder in the block is an EXAMPLE, not a runtime fallback: when instantiating it is COPIED into the IPlaceholderContentWidget of the instance and comes to belong to the consumer - WfCovPriceTag1 keeps the copy next to its note and WfCovPriceTag2 deletes it with a `delete`. It pairs with tests/jobs-odc/block-events-two-instances.json (two instances on the SAME screen, linked by event) and tests/jobs-odc/block-events-nested.json (the event going up two levels): those prove the EVENT, this one proves the REUSE.

ops._why: 2. the other axis of reuse: a parameter carries a VALUE, a placeholder carries CONTENT. Each consumer puts its own.

EXAMPLE content of the block. It is not a runtime fallback: when instantiating, the platform COPIES it into the IPlaceholderContentWidget of the instance and from then on it belongs to the consumer, who edits or deletes it (visible in the dump of the three instances)

8. the THIRD instance of WfCovPriceTag, now by visual authoring and DIRECT on the screen: `:Input` for the arguments and `<slot name="Footnote">` for the placeholder. Same block, two authoring paths, two levels on the same screen.
READ BACK: the optional input really kept the DefaultValue
the block's placeholder, with the example content in it
instancia 1 dentro do bloco: Amount = Premium
instance 2 in the SAME parent: Amount = Deductible. Same block, another argument.
a instancia 2 escreveu: Value = "USD"

THE LESSON: the IArgument EXISTS in instance 1 too - the platform creates one per parameter when instantiating - only without a Value. Inheriting the default is not having no argument, it is having an empty argument; which is why the `usages` of Currency counts the same 3 arguments as that of Amount.
screen 1: literal
screen 2: expression over a screen variable. The same block, two calling contracts.
the instance born from the fragment, with the name from the id: Arguments 4 and PlaceholdersContent 1, like the native ones
THE CORE OF THE PROOF: 3 instances of the same block - two inside IMobileBlock:WfCovPolicyCard (no IMobileScreen in the path) and one inside IMobileScreen:WfCovPolicySummary
THE OTHER CORE: 2 instances of the same block in DIFFERENT SCREENS
mandatory input: one argument per instance
optional input: the SAME 3 arguments as Amount, even though one instance inherits the default - the count does not tell an empty argument from a written one (see the get above)
the placeholder has consumers too: one IPlaceholderContentWidget per instance, the content that each one puts inside it
the two instances side by side: WfCovPriceTag1 with the copy of the example + its note, WfCovPriceTag2 with only its own
the inside of the visual instance: the `<slot>` became the content of the placeholder, next to the copy of the example
